- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+3% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 1–2% in next 3–5 days to align with mean reversion.
- If sentiment is neutral or slightly positive (avg > -0.1) and model shows persistent downward bias, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to capture sentiment-driven upside.
- Model frequently underestimates true price peaks in 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile (±0.3 or higher); add 0.5–1.0% buffer to forecast for high-sentiment periods.
- When sentiment turns positive after a prolonged negative streak, model often lags; shift forecast upward by 0.5–1.0% in next 2–3 days to reflect sentiment momentum.
- Avoid overfitting to recent 3-day highs; if model forecasts peak too early (within 1–2 days of true peak), reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% to avoid premature overvaluation.
